findings.title: Default Tiny ImageNet recovery loses eligibility while its completion marker is absent.
findings.trigger: An actual successful download through the canonical default Tiny URL has a completion marker. Delete only one annotated validation PNG, keeping training, validation directories, annotations and another validation image intact. Either a recovery receives an archive still missing that PNG, or a second constructor starts while the first recovery owns the download flock and is awaiting its HTTP body.
findings.actual: The downloader correctly unlinks the stale marker under flock. tiny_imagenet.DataSource then uses that marker as its sole default-download eligibility check before reaching the downloader. After failed readiness, every subsequent constructor raises ValueError asking for download_url even when the default source now serves the complete archive. During live recovery, the contender raises the same ValueError immediately instead of waiting for the existing lock. The original owner can complete successfully, but the concurrent client has already failed.
findings.expected: A root previously downloaded from the default URL can retry after an incomplete recovery when its source is restored. A concurrent constructor waits for the active recovery and rechecks the repaired root, without another download. Failed or incomplete recovery must still leave no completion marker. Ordinary incomplete manually prepared native roots, unknown classes and offline reuse retain their existing accepted behavior.
findings.impact: Failed default-URL recovery leaves an otherwise recoverable dataset persistently unusable without manual intervention or a new configuration. Concurrent client initialization can fail while the correct default-URL recovery is in progress.

reproduction.method: Use real localhost HTTP, requests, ZIP extraction, native annotations and actual constructors/samples. Assert every production request uses https://cs231n.stanford.edu/tiny-imagenet-200.zip, dispatching only that HTTP request to the local fixture. The minimal reproduction does not patch DataSource.download, _locate_layout, readiness or flock. Threading gates only the fixture HTTP body. Run the same two cases with a configured URL as passing controls.
sequential_steps: Initial default-URL construction downloads once; both training classes and two label-1 validation samples decode to finite tensors; the canonical .complete marker exists.
Delete only val/images/z2.PNG. Serve the same native archive without z2.PNG. Recovery requests the archive again, raises the required-artifact RuntimeError and leaves no completion marker.

Restore the server's complete archive and construct again. Actual: ValueError at tiny_imagenet.py:117, HTTP count stays 2, zero successful retry constructors. Expected: request 3 restores the PNG and publishes completion.
concurrent_steps: Initial default-URL download completes; delete only z2.PNG.
Start a real constructor and pause the second HTTP body after response headers. Its real flock is held and the completion marker is absent.

Start the second constructor, then release the body and join both. Actual: one successful constructor, one ValueError from tiny_imagenet.py:117, two total HTTP requests. Expected: both constructors succeed with two total requests.
reproduction.results_both_versions: Python 3.13.16 and 3.14.8: the two default-URL cases fail, the two otherwise identical configured-URL cases pass; no skips or warnings.
reproduction.broader_independent_confirmation: 99 independent/public-behavior cases on each version: 97 pass and two default-URL recovery cases fail. The smaller four-case reproduction independently confirms the captured product ValueError without lock instrumentation.
